cluster_title: Actor identity, continuity, mandate, and explicit non-identity
supporting_cases: Koto Tangah V2; Tiku V3 (2 independently-built cases)
related_nonfailure_evidence: Painan mandate uncertainty (signatory authority not fully verified); Natal local-signatory uncertainty (5 granular actors, possible_same_actor flag between March/October signatories, never resolved); Sillida neighboring-ruler representation (Bajang/Indrapura/Trosang ceding Sillida's own territory with no documented mandate basis) -- all PASSED their own case's validator without triggering a FAIL, because each artifact used ad hoc extension fields (mandate_status/continuity_status/faction_status) not defined in Draft V2 itself
proposed_model_layer: Actor Identity Rules extension (Draft V2 section 4) -- NOT a new entity class; a set of optional, structured fields on the existing Actor entity
risk_if_ignored: Every future case will independently reinvent ad hoc mandate/continuity bookkeeping fields (already happening identically across V2/V3/V4), producing four non-interoperable local conventions instead of one shared, auditable field set; a future generalized validator cannot check actor-identity discipline consistently without a common field definition
risk_if_added: A structured field set could tempt future artifact authors to treat 'continuity asserted' as equivalent to 'continuity proven' if the field's own semantics are not carefully scoped as OPTIONAL, RESEARCHER-ASSERTED metadata, not a verified fact; risk of the field itself becoming a de facto identity claim over time
counterexamples: None found across V1-V4 where the CURRENT absence of this field caused an outright modeling failure beyond the two cited FAILs -- Painan, Natal, and Sillida's own mandate-uncertainty situations were representable via free-text notes without a structured field, suggesting the field is a QUALITY-OF-AUDIT improvement more than a strict representational necessity in those three cases
notes: Both member failures are the SAME underlying gap manifesting in opposite directions (Koto Tangah: attempted-and-flagged bridge; Tiku: deliberately-not-bridged-and-still-unflagged) -- this symmetry is itself evidence the gap is structural, not case-specific phrasing. Per the plan's own CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED rule ('same structural gap appears in at least two independently built cases'), this cluster qualifies without needing the severity-based alternate trigger.

member_failures: FAIL-05 (Tiku T-04, toll exemption); FAIL-09 (Sillida T-06, salimoet relinquishment)
supporting_cases: Tiku V3; Sillida V4 (2 independently-built cases)
related_nonfailure_evidence: Natal's own 1641-adjacent material (none directly on-point); no other case's frozen ledger surfaced a comparable rights-release act that was successfully represented without this gap
proposed_model_layer: A structured RightModification/CommercialPrivilege action vocabulary (candidate actions: GRANTS/WAIVES/RELEASES/REVOKES/RENEWS/EXEMPTS), evaluated against a minimal field-extension alternative before deciding between an object model and new relation types -- see changeset ledger CF-02
risk_if_ignored: Every future commercial/fiscal-instrument case (a plausible recurring source-material shape across this project's remaining unexamined episodes) will hit the same representational wall and require its own case-specific workaround, each slightly differently worded, defeating cross-case comparability of fiscal-relationship findings
risk_if_added: A dedicated rights/privileges object model is the largest schema surface-area change proposed in this synthesis; risk of over-engineering a general-purpose fiscal-rights ontology from only 2 confirmed cases, when a narrower directional field on COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM might suffice -- see CF-02 alternatives analysis
counterexamples: Sillida T-04 (third-party fine) was INITIALLY considered for this cluster given its shared RELATION_TYPE_FAILURE label, but on closer reading its own historical shape (a punitive third-party arbitration outcome, not a voluntarily-granted-then-released commercial privilege) does not match the GRANTS/WAIVES/RELEASES pattern -- reclassified to FCL-07 instead. This reclassification is itself evidence against naively clustering by failure_type label alone.
notes: Both member failures are represented today via the SAME workaround pattern: model only the standing right (via the existing, correctly-directed relation type), leave the release/exemption act itself unmodeled. This consistent workaround across two independent artifact authors (constructed in separate turns) is itself corroborating evidence for the gap's structural nature.

member_failures: FAIL-01 (Natal T-06, institutional hesitation); FAIL-02 (Koto Tangah T-01, institutional presence)
supporting_cases: Natal V1; Koto Tangah V2 (2 independently-built cases)
related_nonfailure_evidence: No third case surfaced either sub-shape; Tiku and Sillida's own institutional actors (VOC, Aceh court) are used throughout without triggering this specific failure, since neither artifact needed to represent a bare institutional STATE or PRESENCE fact in isolation from a directed action
generalization_status: STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED (downgraded from an initially-plausible CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED reading -- see notes)
proposed_model_layer: Undetermined pending further design work: EITHER one common InstitutionalObservation model, OR two separate models (InstitutionalStateObservation for internal uncertainty; InstitutionalPresenceObservation for bare presence-establishment) -- this synthesis does not resolve which, per the plan's own explicit instruction to determine this as an open question
risk_if_ignored: Two structurally distinct institutional facts (an institution's internal uncertainty about an existing claim, versus an institution merely being present somewhere) continue to be conflated or force-fit into observations that do not cleanly distinguish them, weakening any future institutional-behavior cross-case analysis
risk_if_added: Building ONE unified model when the two sub-shapes actually need different fields (Natal's hesitation needs a 'decision pending' status; Koto Tangah's presence needs a 'presence established, no accompanying claim' status) risks a model too generic to be useful for either, or one that silently conflates 'uncertain' with 'merely present'
counterexamples: None -- both member failures are the only two institutional-state/presence-shaped failures found across the frozen material
notes: Although this cluster technically meets the CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED bar of 'two independently built cases,' this synthesis deliberately downgrades it to STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED because the two failures are NOT the same structural gap -- Natal's is about institutional UNCERTAINTY over an already-accepted claim; Koto Tangah's is about bare institutional PRESENCE with no claim at all. Treating them as one CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED cluster risks designing a single change that solves neither well. Further single-case design exploration is recommended before elevation to CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED.

cluster_title: Ambiguous spatial feature (fort/mine versus wider territory)
related_nonfailure_evidence: Sillida V4 independently tested the SAME underlying spatial-precision question (mine versus wider territory, plus 4 additional distinct location objects: island, second territory, gold-vein boundary, destroyed settlement) using ONLY the existing Draft V2 Location entity model, with ZERO stress-test failure on any of its 6 location distinctions (Sillida stress test T-05, T-15 both PASSED)
generalization_status: REQUIRES_MORE_EVIDENCE (downgraded from the initially-suggested STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED grouping)
proposed_model_layer: No new model layer proposed at this time -- Sillida's own success suggests the existing Location entity model (with its Port/Fort/Mine subtype attribute) is adequate WHEN the underlying sources support the distinction
risk_if_ignored: If genuinely treated as REQUIRES_MORE_EVIDENCE and left unaddressed, a future case with similarly ambiguous fort/territory sources (plausible, since VOC-era place-naming conventions are inconsistent project-wide) could reproduce the same failure -- but this is a SOURCE limitation, not a MODEL limitation, so 'ignoring' it means directing future effort toward source re-examination, not ontology change
risk_if_added: Adding a new spatial-ambiguity field (source_place_expression / feature_type_confidence, per candidate CF-04) when the existing model already works in a richer, harder case (Sillida) risks building an unused, redundant field that duplicates what researcher notes already capture
counterexamples: Sillida V4's own 6-location, zero-failure spatial model is a direct counterexample demonstrating the CURRENT Draft V2 Location model is sufficient when source material permits clean separation -- this is the decisive piece of evidence for the downgrade
notes: This is the clearest case in this synthesis where comparing evidence ACROSS cases changes the initial classification: Koto Tangah's own failure looked, in isolation, like a plausible candidate for a general spatial-ambiguity extension (as the task's own initial classification suggested, grouping it with other 'STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED' items) -- but Sillida's own independently-built, harder spatial-disambiguation case succeeding with the SAME existing model is strong evidence the gap is Koto Tangah's own source material, not Draft V2's Location entity. Recommend a future philological check on Vogel's 'Refort' usage (already proposed in the Koto Tangah V2 audit itself) before any ontology change is considered here.

cluster_title: Resistance target (object of resistance versus object of the relation)
related_nonfailure_evidence: The frozen interpretive ledger contains multiple resistance_candidate=PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED rows across Batches I1-I11 (a full project-wide count is out of this synthesis's own read-only scope, but is recommended as a researcher follow-up, see decision ledger) -- if several of those also have a resistance target distinct from the relation's own object, this would independently corroborate the cluster beyond Tiku alone
proposed_model_layer: An annotation-level extension only (resistance remains research-only, never promoted to a relation, per the task's own explicit and repeated hard rule) -- candidate: a resistance_target_actor_id field alongside the existing resistance_candidate field
risk_if_ignored: A resistance value could be silently misread (by a future researcher, a future public-display designer, or a future generalized validator) as describing resistance TOWARD the relation's own object, when the source actually documents resistance toward a DIFFERENT actor entirely -- this is a genuine risk of a 'serious false historical claim,' the plan's own alternate CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED trigger, even though only one case has formally failed on it so far
risk_if_added: A target-actor field on a research-only annotation is low schema risk (it does not touch the relation-type or entity-type vocabulary at all) but could be over-engineered with additional fields (resistance_target_institution_ids, resistance_scope) beyond what the single confirmed case actually demonstrates a need for
counterexamples: None found within Tiku's own material; the field's necessity elsewhere in the project is inferred, not yet directly confirmed
notes: Elevated to STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED (not merely REQUIRES_MORE_EVIDENCE) despite only one confirmed case, because the public-display risk (Draft V2 section 9 maps interpretive_status=CONTESTED and related resistance signals toward public categories) makes a silent misattribution a genuine historical-accuracy risk, not merely an academic completeness gap -- directly invoking the plan's own severity-based CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED alternate trigger as a reason for priority, even while the strict two-case count is not yet met.

related_nonfailure_evidence: The Batang Capas rows (118, 126, Vogel 1690) cited in the plan as comparison material are the SAME source rows already incorporated into the Sillida V4 artifact itself -- there is currently no INDEPENDENTLY untested case in this project's frozen scope that would supply a second, separate confirmation
generalization_status: STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED (flagged for elevated researcher priority despite single-case, non-independent evidence -- see notes)
proposed_model_layer: Undetermined pending researcher decision between: (a) a structured CommandRelationship/operation object (candidate relation types DIRECTS_OPERATION_BY / DEPLOYS_GROUP_IN / COMMANDS_UNIT, paired with annotations dependency_status/coercion_status/ability_to_refuse/political_intent/voice_availability/constrained_agency), or (b) continuing the current observation-only workaround with a more formally structured (but still non-relational) EffectiveControlObservation extension
risk_if_ignored: This project's own historical material involves coerced/enslaved labor at multiple points (the Sillida mine's own workforce, referenced in both the 1687 rows and structurally implied by the mine's operation across the whole 1648-1737+ span) -- if this gap is never addressed, every future case touching coerced labor inherits the same representational silence, systematically under-representing a historically significant and ethically weighty category of actor
risk_if_added: A dedicated command/constrained-agency relation type or object is the single riskiest proposed change in this synthesis if designed carelessly: it must NEVER be usable to encode voluntary alliance or consent (the task's own explicit hard rule), so any implementation requires unusually careful controlled-vocabulary design to prevent misuse in a direction that would minimize historical coercion
counterexamples: None -- this is a genuinely novel finding with no counterexample of successful representation anywhere in V1-V4
notes: Despite having only ONE case-level failure and that evidence not being independently corroborated by a second, separately-built case (both 1687 rows are already inside the same Sillida artifact), this synthesis elevates FCL-06 to STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED on severity grounds alone, consistent with the plan's own explicit alternate CROSS_CASE_REQUIRED trigger ('one gap would otherwise create serious false historical claims'): silently omitting or, worse, mischaracterizing coerced/enslaved persons' own agency is a serious historical-accuracy and ethical risk regardless of how many cases have so far surfaced it. This is the single highest-priority item in this synthesis's own researcher-decision package.

cluster_title: Dispute settlement, fine, and third-party benefit
related_nonfailure_evidence: Koto Tangah's own 1679-analog material (per that case's own audit) did not include a comparable third-party-fine-adjudication episode; no other case's frozen ledger surfaced one either
proposed_model_layer: A structured DisputeSettlement/FineAllocation/ArbitrationDecision object (candidate fields: disputing_actor_ids, mediating_actor_ids, paying_actor_ids, receiving_actor_ids, resource_or_object, amount_or_share_as_written, settlement_date, source_document_ids) evaluated against forcing settlement into an existing toll/lease/monopoly relation type (explicitly rejected per the task's own hard rule)
risk_if_ignored: A recurring VOC institutional pattern -- adjudicating a local dispute and capturing a disproportionate share of the resulting settlement -- cannot be tracked or compared across cases without a dedicated representation, understating a potentially systematic colonial extraction mechanism this project's own research otherwise aims to surface
risk_if_added: A dedicated dispute-settlement object risks proliferation if scoped too broadly (e.g. absorbing ordinary bilateral treaty negotiations that are already well-served by NEGOTIATES_WITH/RECONCILES_WITH) -- must be scoped specifically to THIRD-PARTY arbitration/fine outcomes, not general dispute resolution
counterexamples: The 1679 Bayang-Sillida dispute itself has a genuine counterexample within the SAME episode: the underlying resource dispute (CONTESTS_RESOURCE_WITH) and its eventual RECONCILES_WITH-style resolution pattern used elsewhere in this project (e.g. Koto Tangah's own 1682 pardon, 1684 reconciliation) DID work without a dedicated settlement object -- only the THIRD-PARTY FINE-COLLECTION dimension specifically resisted representation
notes: Reclassified from an initial, loose grouping near FCL-02 (both share the RELATION_TYPE_FAILURE label) into its own distinct cluster, since the underlying historical mechanism (third-party punitive arbitration) is structurally different from voluntary rights-relinquishment. Single-case evidence, but the pattern (VOC capturing outsized shares of dispute settlements) is plausible enough to recur that this synthesis recommends STRONGLY_RECOMMENDED rather than REQUIRES_MORE_EVIDENCE.
